question: Which phonemes are placed on the hands, branches, heart, breasts, and vital breath in this stage of the Malini installation?
premises: Ṭha is placed on the two hands, and ja and ña are placed on the branches.
Jra and ṭa are associated with the trident and skull-cup, while pa, cha, and la are placed on the heart and breasts.
Sa joined with visarga is identified with the life-force.
inference: The installation links phonemes not only to body parts but also to divine attributes and the vital principle.
uncertainties: The form jraṭau is unusual and may reflect a compressed or transmitted cluster.
The exact referent of śākhā, whether fingers or extended limbs, is not explicit.
plain_english: Ṭha is placed on the two hands, and ja and ña on the branches. Jra and ṭa are linked with the trident and skull-cup. Pa, cha, and la are placed on the heart and breasts, with milk and mā, and sa joined with visarga is identified as the life-force.
